newsitem.title: JAPAN: China WTO entry talk in final stage--Ruggiero.
newsitem.headline: China WTO entry talk in final stage--Ruggiero.

text.p: The head of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on Friday expressed optimism over the possibility of China joining the global trade body, saying that decade-long talks with the communist giant may be soon coming to an end.

"It seems to me that we are approaching the final stages of negotiations," director-general Renato Ruggiero told a news conference in Tokyo, where he is on a six-day visit to meet government officials and top business leaders.
Despite much progress in talks held in Geneva this month, he said that all the parties involved, including China, did not want to give any specific time frame for its possible entry.
He said that there were still issues that had to be resolved, but did not clarify what they were.

Beijing's bid to join the WTO has been held up partly because it wants to join on the terms accorded to developing countries, which are considered to be easier. This would allow Beijing more time to adjust its trade practices to the WTO's internationally agreed upon rules for global free trade.
Some Western nations, including the United States, insist that China's economy is too big to be afforded developing country treatment.
Ruggiero said that negotiations on China's possible entry will continue in the positive spirit shared during the recent negotiations which made much progress.
The WTO chief is scheduled to visit China in mid-April to try to help speed up Beijing's admission.

"We need China in the WTO because we want to make a universal trade system and this is only possible if China becomes a member of the WTO. We both have an interest in China becoming a member of the WTO under the right conditions," Ruggiero told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
In his meeting with Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato on Wednesday, Ruggiero expressed hope that Chinese leaders will show strong political commitment to speed up negotiations on China's membership.

A ministry official suggested that Ruggiero's remark meant that he wanted Chinese leaders to send a message to its negotiators to speed up negotiations despite apparent reluctance among some groups in China on the issue.
The WTO head also said that prospects were encouraging for China's archrival Taiwan and Russia to join the world trade group.
